target.title: fix(feishu): deliver visible notice on reply-session init conflict (#108320)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the Feishu channel, when a reply-session initialization conflict occurs (the load-bearing error `reply session initialization conflicted for ...`, raised after the bounded CAS retry is exhausted), `handleFeishuMessage` only logged the error and **silently dropped the inbound message**. The user received no feedback at all — the message vanished.

This is a behavioral gap versus the Slack, Signal, and Discord channels, which all deliver a visible terminal notice to the user on this exact condition. #108320 reports the Feishu silent-drop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's `handleFeishuMessage` catch block previously fell through to the generic "failed to dispatch" error log with no user-facing message. The fix detects the reply-session init conflict (via a local `FEISHU_REPLY_SESSION_INIT_CONFLICT_MESSAGE_RE`, matching the per-channel convention where each channel defines its own local regex) and, on match, calls the real `sendMessageFeishu` with a clear notice:

> ⚠️ Couldn't process this message because the session stayed busy. Please try again in a moment.

The notice **reuses the fully-resolved delivery parameters** — the effective config, the resolved `replyToMessageId`, the `replyInThread` flag, and the pre-dispatch target — captured immediately before dispatch, so the notice lands exactly where a normal reply would (including P2P direct-message threads and topic sessions) instead of falling back to a plain chat-level message. The notice delivery is wrapped in its own try/catch so a send failure is logged but never re-drops the original message.

## User Impact

Feishu users who hit a transient reply-session init conflict now get a visible, actionable notice in their conversation (or thread) instead of a silent drop. No behavior change for the success path or for other error types.

## Evidence

Regression coverage in `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts`, forcing the real `handleFeishuMessage` dispatch path to reject with the conflict error:

- **Synthetic direct message** ("delivers a visible notice when reply-session init conflict exhausts its retry"): notice delivered to `chat:oc_dm`, replying to `msg-conflict`, with the "session stayed busy" text.
- **P2P direct-message thread** ("delivers the reply-session conflict notice inside P2P direct-message threads"): notice delivered to `chat:oc_dm` with `replyToMessageId: "msg-conflict-thread-root"` and `replyInThread: true` — proving the resolved thread target is reused.

```bash
pnpm vitest run extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  96 passed (96)
```

Branch is rebased onto latest `origin/main` (head `db2fd7fe`); diff is `extensions/feishu/src/bot.ts` and `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts`.

### What was not tested

The conflict is a race condition (CAS contention during session init) that cannot be deterministically forced in a live channel E2E, and this contributor environment has no Feishu app credentials for a live send. Proof is the dispatch-path regression tests above plus parity with the existing Slack/Signal/Discord implementations, which use the same detect-and-notice pattern and the same notice text.
